task.description: WF-02 Step 5. Independently re-run the suite and re-derive every one of REQ-023's 5 acceptance criteria against the ACTUAL shipped code and real database state -- not against TEST-RUNNER's report, not against any prior gate's verdict, and not against the design artefact's claims about itself. Per core-directives.md, RELEASE-VALIDATOR re-runs rather than trusting the report alone; that is the entire reason this step exists. Also check docs/requirements.yaml and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml for staleness relative to what actually shipped. Note this run has produced an unusually large forwarded-issue set (ISS-0012 through ISS-0020, plus updates to ISS-0011, ISS-0015 and ISS-0017) -- verify none of them is in fact a blocker on REQ-023's own acceptance criteria that was mis-classified as incidental.
acceptance_criteria: the full suite is independently re-run (multiple times, given ISS-0011's characterised ~7.5% flake rate) with real output quoted
each of REQ-023's 5 acceptance criteria is verified against actual code/DB state, with the evidence for each stated separately
docs/requirements.yaml and docs/status/requirement_status.yaml are checked for staleness relative to what shipped
the forwarded-issue set is reviewed for any mis-classified blocker
a release decision record is written to docs/status/

result.summary: WF-02 Step 5 release validation for REQ-023: PASS. Everything below was re-derived independently -- TEST-RUNNER's report, the earlier gates' verdicts and the design artefact's claims about itself were all treated as unverified. SUITE (re-run 17 times by this validator, not once): 11 unpinned + 6 at --seed 0. 14 runs clean at the reference figure 'Result: 198 passed (4 properties, 194 tests)'; 3 runs red. Aggregating ExUnit's failure-header pattern across all 17 captured logs yields EXACTLY ONE distinct failing test in the whole corpus, and every red run reported 'Failed: 1 test'. In all three cases it is byte-identical: '1) test method short-circuit -- no DB query at all for a non-write method a GET request issues no Ecto query at all (method short-circuit, no DB round-trip) (Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatusTest)' at test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:121, failing on 'refute_received :query_fired, "expected no Ecto query for a GET request"', stacktrace test/letflow/plugs/tenant_status_test.exs:136 -- i.e. exactly ISS-0011 / GH #65, pre-existing from REQ-021. Run 3's log captures the race in the act (foreign queries against tenants, approvals, groups, users bracketing the failure block). Seed 0 failed once in 6, independently reproducing for a THIRD time (after Step 3b and Step 4) that --seed 0 is not a deterministic baseline. NO other test failed in any run, so no genuine new signal appeared. Observed rate 3/17 = 17.6% vs ISS-0011's 40-run 7.5% -- recorded as a small-sample observation, not a correction; the 40-run figure remains the better estimate. Baseline reconciles exactly: 161 before REQ-023 + 37 from REQ-023's own two test files (run alone: 'Result: 37 passed') = 198. GATES: 'MIX_TEST_PARTITION=2 MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors' exit 0, and again with --force (real recompile of all 37 files, not a no-op) exit 0; 'mix format --check-formatted' exit 0. CRITERIA, each established separately against actual code / the real Postgres catalog / a command actually run: (1) SIX MIGRATIONS + :prefix + CLEAN APPLY -- verified behaviourally, not from migration source. Inserted a real tenant, provisioned schema tenant_f10f992c6da64fdea7e395e99429193c via TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1, then invoked REQ-022's own replay_migrations/1, which returned {:ok, [20260816120001..120006]}. Inspected the catalog from a SEPARATE psql process (docker exec letflow-postgres-1 psql -d letflow_test2) so the evidence does not depend on the BEAM process that wrote it: information_schema.tables for that schema lists exactly event_idempotency, event_payload_store, events, events_archive, instance_projections, instance_sequence, schema_migrations. Negative control: public gained NO event-store table (still only approvals, groups, schema_migrations, tenant_role, tenant_schemas, tenants, transition_events, users), confirming the 'if prefix() do' guard works. All six files pass prefix: prefix() on create table and on every index, and all six are registered in TenantProvisioning's @tenant_scoped_migration_manifest (registration is the mandatory second half -- an unregistered guarded migration is inert). (2) COMPOSITE PK -- from the live catalog, not from the migration's annotations: information_schema.table_constraints JOIN key_column_usage returns events_pkey with ordinal_position 1 = event_id, 2 = created_at; pg_indexes shows 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX events_pkey ON <schema>.events USING btree (event_id, created_at)'. events_archive independently carries the same shape. (3) NO UPDATE PATH ON events -- verified by BEAM module reflection rather than by grepping for an absent string: Letflow.EventStore.Event.__info__(:functions) minus Ecto's __-prefixed entries is exactly [insert_changeset: 2]; function_exported?(Event, :update_changeset, 2) => false and (:changeset, 2) => false; grep for Repo.|update_changeset|update_all|force_change|update( finds no executable hit in event.ex (its two hits are doc text). Moduledoc carries the required statement citing 0003 Decision C point 1 verbatim. Checked deliberately rather than waved past: InstanceProjection DOES export update_changeset/2, but criterion 3 constrains the events module only and instance_projections is by design a mutable projection, with its moduledoc calling out the exception. (4) SIDECAR UNIQUE INDEX + SUPERSESSION -- pg_indexes: 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_event_idempotency_key ON <schema>.event_idempotency USING btree (idempotency_key)'. Single-enforcement-point claim independently confirmed: no index on events or events_archive covers idempotency_key. IdempotencyRecord's moduledoc states it supersedes event_store.md's Open Question #1 two-phase check, citing 0003 Decision C point 2(b); the name choice event_idempotency is cited as the requirement permits. (5) instance_projections SCOPE -- moduledoc's '## Scope (REQ-023 acceptance criterion 5)' section states the schema is REQ-023's and that meaningful population at instance start is EE-01/S3 territory, and enumerates the engine-owned columns deliberately not created, which matches the live catalog (only instance_id, tenant_id, status, last_event_seq, started_at, updated_at + idx_proj_status). STALENESS: docs/requirements.yaml REQ-023 is status: in_progress, correct at Step 5 (DOC-UPDATER flips at Step 6); its description and all five criteria match what shipped; grepped and confirmed the stale 'tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returns []' claim ISS-0017 tracks has NOT spread into requirements.yaml. docs/status/requirement_status.yaml carries exactly one REQ-023 event ('started', ORCH, 2026-08-16T15:38:45Z) at line 1787 of 1804 -- correct at Step 5, append-only convention intact, and its recorded 161-test baseline reconciles with the 198 seen now. Neither file is stale. ISSUE SET (ISS-0012..0020 + updates to 0011/0015/0017) reviewed as a real check: NO mis-classified blocker. ISS-0013 checked specifically as instructed -- event_retention_policies is genuinely outside all five criteria (criterion 1 enumerates exactly six tables and it is not among them; criteria 2-5 name only events, the sidecar, instance_projections), its consumer is REQ-026's archive/1 which this run does not build, and nothing in lib/letflow/event_store/ reads it, so nothing REQ-023 ships can fail on its absence; adding it here would have been scope creep against REQ-023's own criteria. ISS-0017 is the only issue that genuinely blocked a criterion (tenant_scoped_migrations/0 previously returned []) -- correctly fixed in-run under Unblock-Everything, and the fix is independently confirmed here by the successful six-version replay; its open residue is design-doc prose only, which no criterion constrains. ISS-0019 was examined closely rather than skimmed because it touches criterion 1's own mechanism: it is an error-PATH shape defect (default arg evaluated outside try/rescue) that changes how a failure is reported, never whether a successful replay succeeds -- and the success path was exercised end-to-end. ISS-0016 was re-derived: .formatter.exs's inputs genuinely omit priv/, so the project format gate never covered the migrations -- but under a scratch-only config with import_deps: [:ecto_sql] (the project's .formatter.exs was NOT modified) all six REQ-023 migrations check clean, exit 0, so no formatting defect was actually shipped and the gap is pre-existing across all 13 migrations. ISS-0012/0014/0015/0018/0020 are documentation, other-requirement scope, test-harness, or rationale-quality concerns touching no criterion; ISS-0020 was read in full to confirm none of its three items asserts a shipped decision is wrong. DB HYGIENE: the one tenant schema created was dropped along with its tenant_schemas registration and tenants row; post-cleanup letflow_test2 shows only 'public', 0 leftover registrations, 0 leftover rv-req023-* tenants. All work confined to the letflow_test2 partition; letflow_test and letflow_dev never touched. No :eaddrinuse abort occurred in any of the 17 runs.

issues.description: NEW (not filed, reported per dispatch instruction): protocol drift between two authoritative docs. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 step 4 instructs the completing agent to update handoffs/registry.json, while this run's dispatch instructs RELEASE-VALIDATOR to leave registry.json alone as ORCH-owned. Followed the run instruction (registry.json untouched) and flagging the discrepancy rather than silently picking a side, per core-directives.md's rule that a doc disagreement is raised as MINOR so it gets fixed at the source. A question about protocol text for ORCH, not a defect in REQ-023.

OBSERVATION on an already-filed issue (ISS-0011, not re-filed): this validator observed 3 failures in 17 runs (17.6%) versus the 7.5% recorded on the 40-run sample. Recorded as small-sample noise, not a correction -- 17 runs is exactly the sample size ISS-0011's own Step 4 UPDATE cautions about, and the 40-run figure remains the better estimate. Substantively it reconfirms the record: one distinct failing test across all 17 logs, and a third independent reproduction of the finding that --seed 0 is not deterministic.

OBSERVATION on an already-filed issue (ISS-0017, not re-filed): its residual doc staleness sits inside REQ-023's OWN design artefact -- lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md lines 46 and 883 state tenant_scoped_migrations/0 returns [], which this same run's Step 2a falsified. Deliberately not edited: it passed the Step 1b hard gate and this validator does not modify gated artefacts. Highlighted as the highest-value item in the forwarded set for a follow-up run, since the next requirement reading this artefact would meet a statement that was already false when it was committed.
